subject: math.AP
name: Three-dimensional Navier–Stokes regularity
statement: For every smooth divergence-free initial velocity on ℝ³ with rapid decay and finite energy, does the unforced incompressible Navier–Stokes equation with positive viscosity have a unique smooth solution for all t ≥ 0?
importance: This is a central obstacle in the mathematical understanding of viscous fluid motion and a Millennium Prize Problem.
status_note: Global finite-energy weak solutions exist, and regularity is known under additional size or integrability assumptions; these do not settle arbitrary smooth data.

subject: math.AP
name: Three-dimensional Euler singularity problem
statement: Can a smooth finite-energy divergence-free initial velocity on ℝ³ produce a finite-time singularity in the unforced incompressible Euler equations, or do all such solutions remain smooth?
importance: It asks whether ideal-fluid vortex stretching can create singularities from smooth data.
status_note: Global regularity is known in two dimensions. Results for lower-regularity data or flows with boundaries do not settle this smooth whole-space question.

references.title: Majda and Bertozzi, Vorticity and Incompressible Flow

subject: math.AP
name: Inviscid surface quasi-geostrophic regularity
statement: For θ₀ ∈ C∞_c(ℝ²), does the solution of ∂ₜθ + u·∇θ = 0, u = ∇⊥(−Δ)^(−1/2)θ, remain smooth for all time, or can a finite-time singularity occur?
importance: SQG is a fundamental active-scalar model for atmospheric fronts and a test case for singularity formation.
status_note: Weak solutions and several conditional criteria are known. Smooth whole-plane global regularity remains unresolved.

references.title: Chae, Constantin and Wu, Inviscid models generalizing the 2D Euler and the surface quasi-geostrophic equations

subject: math.AP
name: Supercritical dissipative SQG regularity
statement: For θ₀ ∈ C∞_c(ℝ²), does ∂ₜθ + ∇⊥(−Δ)^(−1/2)θ·∇θ + (−Δ)^(1/4)θ = 0 have a smooth solution for all time?
importance: It tests whether weak fractional diffusion can prevent nonlinear front formation.
status_note: The critical dissipation (−Δ)^(1/2) is globally regular; this entry fixes the genuinely supercritical exponent 1/4.

references.title: Caffarelli and Vasseur, Drift diffusion equations with fractional diffusion and the quasi-geostrophic equation

subject: math.AP
name: Global regularity of two-dimensional ideal MHD
statement: For smooth divergence-free periodic initial velocity u and magnetic field b on T², do the incompressible ideal MHD equations ∂ₜu+u·∇u−b·∇b+∇p=0 and ∂ₜb+u·∇b−b·∇u=0 remain smooth for all time?
importance: This asks whether magnetic coupling can cause singularities even in two-dimensional ideal fluids.
status_note: Neither viscosity nor magnetic resistivity is present. Regularity results for dissipative or specially structured data do not settle arbitrary smooth periodic data.

references.title: Cao and Wu, Global regularity for the 2D MHD equations with mixed partial dissipation and magnetic diffusion

subject: math.AP
name: Smooth whole-plane inviscid Boussinesq regularity
statement: For smooth compactly supported initial temperature and smooth divergence-free finite-energy initial velocity on ℝ², do ∂ₜu+u·∇u+∇p=θe₂ and ∂ₜθ+u·∇θ=0 remain smooth for all time?
importance: The Boussinesq system is a basic model for buoyancy-driven flow and a proxy for three-dimensional vortex stretching.
status_note: Singularity constructions with boundaries or less regular data do not settle smooth whole-plane data.

references.title: Global smooth solutions of the damped Boussinesq equations with a class of large initial data
Elgindi and Jeong, Finite-time Singularity Formation for Strong Solutions to the Boussinesq System

subject: math.AP
name: Large-data smooth Boltzmann evolution
statement: For the spatially periodic three-dimensional Boltzmann equation with hard-sphere collisions, does every smooth strictly positive initial distribution with finite mass, energy and entropy and sufficiently fast velocity decay generate a global classical solution?
importance: It would establish a full large-data mathematical theory of dilute-gas evolution.
status_note: Renormalized global weak solutions and perturbative classical solutions are known; arbitrary far-from-equilibrium smooth data remain outside that theory.

references.title: Villani, A review of mathematical topics in collisional kinetic theory

subject: math.AP
name: Inhomogeneous Coulomb Landau global regularity
statement: Does every smooth positive initial distribution on T³_x × ℝ³_v with finite mass, energy and entropy and suitable velocity decay give a global smooth solution of the spatially inhomogeneous nonrelativistic Landau equation with Coulomb interaction?
importance: This is a central regularity problem for kinetic models of plasma collisions.
status_note: The spatially homogeneous Coulomb problem has recent global regularity results. Spatial inhomogeneity and arbitrary large data are essential here; known continuation criteria are conditional.

references.title: Henderson, Snelson and Tarfulea, Local existence, lower mass bounds, and a new continuation criterion for the Landau equation

subject: math.AP
name: De Giorgi conjecture in dimension eight
statement: If u ∈ C²(ℝ⁸) solves Δu = u³−u, satisfies |u|<1, and has ∂u/∂x₈ > 0 everywhere, must u depend on only one linear coordinate?
importance: It links diffuse-interface PDEs with the geometry and rigidity of minimal hypersurfaces.
status_note: The full conjecture is proved in dimensions two and three and under additional asymptotic hypotheses up to dimension eight; counterexamples exist from dimension nine onward.

references.title: Phase transitions with bounded index: Parallels to De Giorgi’s conjecture

subject: math.AP
name: Nonradial soliton resolution for the critical wave equation
statement: For every global solution of ∂ₜ²u−Δu−u⁵=0 on ℝ³ whose Ḣ¹ × L² norm is uniformly bounded, does its evolution as t→∞ split in the energy topology into free radiation and finitely many asymptotically decoupled rescaled, translated traveling stationary solutions?
importance: It seeks a complete description of long-time behavior in a fundamental nonlinear dispersive model.
status_note: Radial cases have strong resolution theorems. The general nonradial decomposition along all large times is the open scope; decompositions only along selected time sequences are weaker.

references.title: Tao, Global behaviour of nonlinear dispersive and wave equations
